EmailTemplate.subject: Thank you for your interest in the School of Music at ASU!
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Dear {!Contact.FirstName},
Thank you for your interest in undergraduate studies at the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts School of Music at ASU. As one of the largest universities in the country, the ASU School of Music awards over $2 million to students annually, providing an excellent education at an unbeatable value. ASU's diverse and innovative community is a perfect complement to the personal attention you will receive in the School of Music. With a population of around 750 students, we offer small class sizes, state-of-the-art facilities and one-on-one instruction from world-renowned faculty. We invite you to consider the ASU School of Music for this important step in your music studies.
If you are interested in applying for fall 2017 admission, please first contact the School of Music Admissions office at musicadmissions@asu.edu to confirm that your desired program is accepting late applications. If you are interested in future study at ASU, please refer to the information below as a guideline for what to expect when you are ready to apply. For an idea of the course requirements for the various degree programs offered, select one of the checksheets accessible by your degree program of interest here.
Tuition and fees at Arizona State University are reasonable, even for non-resident students. Financial aid including academic scholarships is available for both Freshman and Transfer applicants. Freshman applicants can use the Freshman Merit Scholarship Estimator to determine the amount they may be eligible to receive. Transfer applicants may learn about the New American University Transfer Scholarship here. In addition, music scholarship assistance is also available and awarded based on audition.
Application Process
Step 1: Apply to ASU Step 2: Submit the School of Music Application
You do not need to be admitted to the university prior to submitting your music application (Step 2) The School of Music is a separate application from the university. Please visit the School of Music Website for more details.
Step 3: Audition and Interview
All applicants must perform an audition to be considered for admission to the School of Music. On-Campus auditions will not be scheduled until all both application are submitted Recorded auditions are acceptable when uploaded online. However, music scholarship consideration is prioritized to those who audition live.
Due to the high volume of applicants we receive each year, we recommend that you plan to apply as early as possible.
Application Deadline
Spring Admission: October 15 for all applicants except those applying to Music Composition. BM Composition applicants: Application and prescreening portfolio must be received by October 1. Please visit our site for more information.
Fall Admission: January 6 for all applicants except those applying to Music Composition. BM Composition: Prescreening portfolio must be received by December 1. Please visit our site for more information.
Audition Dates and Information
For complete audition dates and audition information please visit the Audition website.
Recorded auditions (in lieu of live auditions) must be uploaded online by November 1 for spring admissions and February 1 for fall admission. CD/DVD audition recordings are not accepted. To be considered for a music scholarship or teaching assistantship, a live, on-campus audition is preferred.
Ad hoc auditions may be scheduled with faculty (required for organ applicants, not available to voice applicants), but must be completed by November 30 for spring admission and February 28 for fall admission.
We welcome you to contact us via email to MusicAdmissions@asu.edu if you have any additional questions. We also encourage you to refer to the School of Music Web site, music.asu.edu, as a resource for your admissions questions.
Sincerely,
Office of Admissions School of Music
Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts Arizona State University
